reference: Independent GNU findutils xargs runs under system Bash in C locale and UTC. Each parity case compares stdout bytes, exit status, diagnostic presence, and private fixture trees through the mandatory isolated submit helper. Children are fixed /bin/sh or /usr/bin/printf commands. Metadata is a separate Bash type/help contract.
coverage: POSIX whitespace splitting, quotes, backslash escapes, empty quoted arguments, and -n batching
-0 NUL-separated arguments, including spaces, an empty argument, and an embedded newline
-I replacement on complete lines with repeated replacement strings and blank-line skipping
-s command-line byte accounting at a two-item boundary
fatal child exit status 255 and early stop
successful -P launches with order-independent child output
Logical line boundaries, trailing-blank continuations, quoting and NUL interactions
Grouping option precedence and bounded command-size failures
Ordinary child error folding and parallel fatal-child cleanup
exclusions: Interactive -p prompting is deferred because the runner does not provide a controlling PTY.
Signal and host-process tests, stress inputs, execution-failure probes, and large ARG_MAX boundaries are outside this bounded review.

The 49 cases retain the draft suite and separately expose small parser, grouping, size, and error boundaries shared by -n, -L, -I and -0; metadata and PTY deferral do not count as GNU operation passes.

cases.purpose: Bash type reports xargs as a builtin and Bash help can find the loadable's documented help topic.
cases.script:
type -t xargs
help xargs >help.txt
printf 'help:available\n'

cases.purpose: Check GNU/POSIX token parsing, including quoted spaces, an escaped blank, an empty quoted argument, and a final short -n batch.
cases.script: printf '%s' 'alpha "two words" three\ four "" tail' | xargs -n 2 /bin/sh -c 'printf "argc=%s\n" "$#"; printf "<%s>\n" "$@"' sh

cases.purpose: Check -0 preserves spaces, empty arguments, and embedded newlines as argument bytes.
cases.script:
printf 'a b\0two words\0\0line
break\0' | xargs -0 -n 2 /bin/sh -c 'printf "argc=%s
" "$#"; printf "<%s>
" "$@"' sh

cases.purpose: Check -I treats each nonblank input line as one replacement value and substitutes every occurrence in a template word.
cases.script:
printf 'two words

end
' | xargs -I '{}' /usr/bin/printf '<%s>
' 'left:{}:{}'

cases.purpose: Check that -L groups nonblank input lines while ordinary blanks within a line still delimit separate arguments.
cases.script:
printf 'one two
three
four five
' | xargs -L 2 /bin/sh -c 'printf "argc=%s
" "$#"; printf "<%s>
" "$@"' sh

cases.purpose: Check -s byte accounting including /bin/sh, its fixed arguments, input arguments, and terminating NUL bytes; the 35-byte cap fits exactly two one-byte items per invocation.
cases.script: printf 'a b c d\n' | xargs -s 35 /bin/sh -c 'printf "batch\n"' sh

cases.purpose: Check GNU's default one invocation on empty input and -r suppression in the same shell process.
cases.script: xargs -r /usr/bin/printf 'ran\n'; xargs /usr/bin/printf 'ran\n'

cases.purpose: Check exit 255 maps to xargs status 124, emits a diagnostic, and prevents later input from being launched.
cases.script:
set +e
printf 'first\nsecond\n' | xargs -n 1 /bin/sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "$1"; exit 255' sh
rc=$?
printf 'xargs-status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check an unterminated input quote is reported as an xargs error and does not execute a command on otherwise empty input.
cases.script:
set +e
printf '"unfinished' | xargs -r /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'
rc=$?
printf 'xargs-status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Exercise -P 2 over four independent invocations. The fixed marker output is identical for every child, so scheduler order cannot affect stdout.
cases.script: printf 'a b c d\n' | xargs -n 1 -P 2 /bin/sh -c 'printf "job\n"' sh

cases.purpose: Exercise -p confirmation and rejection with one harmless fixed child command.
cases.reason: A meaningful -p check needs a controlling PTY to provide bounded y/n responses. The fixture runner supplies no PTY, so defer until a future disposable VM/PTY driver can feed fixed answers and verify whether the child marker runs.

	three\\ four '"'"''"'"'

five six' | xargs -L 2 /bin/sh -c 'printf "argc=%s\n" "$#"; printf "<%s>\n" "$@"' sh

cases.purpose: Under -0, each NUL record counts toward -L; embedded newlines, empty records, quotes and blanks are literal.

cases.purpose: The 23-byte fixed printf command plus two one-byte words and their NULs fits exactly at -s 27; -L preserves both arguments.
cases.script:

c
' | xargs -L 1 -s 27 /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'

cases.purpose: GNU -L implies exit on an oversized logical batch rather than splitting it.

printf '%b' 'aaa bbb ccc
d
' | xargs -L 2 -s 32 /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'
rc=$?
printf 'xargs-status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

' | xargs -L 2 -r /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'

cases.purpose: GNU drops an empty quoted argument at EOF without a terminating delimiter; preserve that observed boundary behavior.
cases.script: printf '%b' '""' | xargs -n 1 /bin/sh -c 'printf "argc=%s\n" "$#"; printf "<%s>\n" "$@"' sh

cases.purpose: Backslashes within quotes are literal under GNU xargs.

	end

cases.purpose: Ordinary nonzero children fold to 123 while remaining batches run, followed by a fresh successful invocation in the same shell.
cases.script:
set +e
printf 'a b c\n' | xargs -n 1 /bin/sh -c 'printf "<%s>\n" "$1"; exit 7' sh
rc=$?
printf 'xargs-status=%s\n' "$rc"
printf 'tail\n' | xargs -n 1 /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Two fixed parallel children both exit 255; diagnostics and 124 folding survive pool cleanup, and a following invocation still runs.
cases.script:
set +e
printf 'a b\n' | xargs -P 2 -n 1 /bin/sh -c 'exit 255' sh
rc=$?
printf 'xargs-status=%s\n' "$rc"
printf 'tail\n' | xargs -n 1 /usr/bin/printf '<%s>\n'
exit "$rc"
